newsitem.title: ZAIRE: More than 100 foreigners trapped in Zaire town.
newsitem.headline: More than 100 foreigners trapped in Zaire town.

text.p: At least 100 foreigners are trapped in the Roman Catholic cathedral of the Zairean town of Bukavu where fighting has raged for days, Zairean rebels said on Friday.
It was not clear what nationality the foreigners were but reporters in the town this week said Belgian and Italian missionaries were still in Bukavu.
The rebels told Reuters correspondent Buchizya Mseteka, inside rebel-held Zaire, that fighters of the former Rwandan Hutu army had been resisting a rebel advance on the town.
"They have one or two artillery batteries," a rebel commander said of the Rwandan fighters.
Bukavu has been the scene of some of the fiercest fighting in eastern Zaire and the Roman Catholic archbishop Christophe Munzihirwa was killed in a military attack there on Tuesday.
Some United Nations staff workers have also died in the fighting.
Hubert Edongo, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees representative in in the Zairean capital Kinshasa, told Reuters on Friday that several local UNHCR workers had been killed in an ambush.
"I don't know how many were killed or who did it, but I know that a convoy was ambushed," he said.
The fighting in Bukavu, part of a broader conflict in eastern Zaire, pits Tutsi ethnic rebels against Zairean troops and Hutu fighters from the former Rwandan army.
The rebels say they hold most of the lakeside town, which is about 30 km (18 miles) north of here. Aid workers say they believe the rebel claims.
